overall: At 4:15 AM ET, Atlanta is sitting at 64.4°F with a running max of 66.2°F and essentially no temperature velocity, consistent with a typical pre-dawn lull. The most notable feature is the extremely high dewpoint of 62.6°F — only 1.8°F below the current air temperature — indicating near-saturated low-level moisture that could promote cloud development and convective activity as daytime heating ramps up.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show solid agreement, clustering tightly between 83.8°F (ECMWF) and 85.4°F (GFS and HRRR), a spread of just ~1.6°F, with NBM splitting the difference at 84.1°F. Both ensemble signals assign low probabilities to the upper tail (87–89°F range at only 5–14%), reinforcing that a dramatic upside surprise appears unlikely.
max_temp_prediction: Today's high should land near 84–85°F, with the tight model consensus centered around 84.5°F serving as the best single estimate. The near-saturated boundary layer is a modest downside risk — afternoon convective cloud cover could limit peak heating and nudge the actual high slightly below the GFS/HRRR 85.4°F guidance toward the ECMWF/NBM lower end. Confidence is moderate-to-good given strong inter-model agreement and ensemble tails both flagged as Tier 4 (Avoid).
